authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Is 1.5x Higher Than In 1972
authored_explainer.hook: By the 1970s, experts warned food would run out; the data reversed that.
says: In 1985, progression to secondary school was 77.8; by 2017 it reached 91.3, 1.2 times higher.
In 1972, cereal production was 1083.7 million metric tons; by 2024 it reached 1644.1 million metric tons, 1.5 times higher.
China has 5.2 million square kilometers of farmland; United States 4.2, Australia 3.6, Brazil 2.4, and Russia 2.2.
authored_explainer.closing: Food output rose without simply adding more farmland.
authored_explainer.question: What changed food production most?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible Renewables And Waste Is 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
authored_explainer.hook: Since 1990, this energy source tripled—and it was not solar or wind.
says: In 1990, combustible renewables and waste was 10.2 % of total energy; by 2024, 30.1 %, 3.0 times higher.
In 1998, access to electricity was 73.2 % of population; by 2024, 91.9 %, 1.3 times higher.
In 1972, methane (ch4) emissions from waste was 903.8 Mt CO2e; by 2024, 1,652 Mt CO2e, 1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: Waste can supply energy while still creating an emissions problem.
authored_explainer.question: Should waste energy count as clean?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth was supposed to accelerate forever; it fell 54% instead.
says: In 1972, rural population was 63.1 % of total population; by 2025, 42.2 %, down to 67 percent of that.
In 1972, population in the largest city was 18.2 % of urban population; by 2025, 16.2 %, barely moved.
In 1972, population growth was 2 annual %; by 2025, 0.91 annual %, down to 46 percent of that.
authored_explainer.closing: Slower growth still adds people, changing how cities must plan.
authored_explainer.question: How should cities plan now?
